items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Celestine, myself, Johnny Lindsay, Ernest Trapani, Lorenzo Teo

ctx.x: Do you remember about, excuse me, what year that was about? Was that...

That could have been about 1910. 1910, when you joined the Silver Leaf. Silver Leaf Band. I was still living in Jefferson Paris. And then I moved to New Orleans in 1911. And I was still with Silver Leaf Band. And Mr. Welch, he was a sickly man and he gave up the coinette playing. And we got over to the fellow by the name of Hippolyte Charles. He played coinette for us a while. And then he gave up the coinette playing and old man Welch came back again. And old man Welch made me to know Celestine. He said he was a…
You had already called it the Tuxedo Band though before you started the tuxedos. Is that right? Yes. And he was a big help to us.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Oh, yeah, now the clarinet player, Lorenzo Tio. See, all of the Tios, all those old men, you know, they've been there, they're professional clarinet players. Them old men, they've been there, but Tio was the... The younger one.

ctx.x: and made a new piece out of the melody line. Yeah. And made clarendina everybody,

and he called it high society. High society. And that's how he could play. I see. Him, George Bacchier, and a fellow called Tio, them as the men who played at the same. Which Tio? Which one, though? Oh, yeah, now the clarinet player, Lorenzo Tio. See, all of the Tios, all those old men, you know, they've been there, they're professional clarinet players. Them old men, they've been there, but Tio was the... The younger one. The guy used to be with Tio in the 20s? Yeah, he used to play with me. He was with us all…
He was with you in what band? Tuxedo. Orchestra or brass band? No, in both.
